GCSE examinations are the mainstay of an English education, with most students following this pathway. The difficulty level of GCSE and IGCSE exams are the same, but the content of GCSE examinations is more English-centred. The series of talks delivered by 8 students traversed a wide array of subjects, each narrating a different facet of personal ambitions, societal aspirations, and the vast potential of human creativity. Joshua Host - Year 12 Rodion Year 12 Sofia Year 12 Laila Year 13 Mohamad Year 12 Mira Year 8 Liam Year 7 Sandiaga Year 8 Mrs. Devika Mankani Divisional Head & Managing Director Regent International School & Chief Positive Psychologist of Fortes Education Residential Trips Students embark on many residential adventures in Secondary and Sixth Form. We have close partnerships with Camps International and Ecoventure ME that offer regional and international trips for students throughout the academic year. Sunmarke also offers The Duke of Edinburgh International Award (DofE International Award) which enriches our students’ lives with practical experiences, life skills and allows them to discover their hidden talents and capabilities. The Duke Of Edinburgh Award The Duke of Edinburgh International Award, founded in 1956 by His Royal Highness the Duke of Edinburgh is the world’s leading youth achievement award, bringing together experiences and life skills to equip young people for life. The concept of the Award is of individual challenge designed to encourage young people between 14 and 25 to develop into responsible, active citizens who will contribute towards society. What’s involved? The Award is voluntary, non-competitive, enjoyable and balanced, and requires students to expend effort over a period of time. There are three levels to the Award: Bronze, Silver and Gold. Young people design their own Award programme, set their own goals and record their own progress. They can choose four categories: Service, Physical Recreation or a Skills activity, or go on an Expedition. Here are some more details of each segment. Service The Award gives students the opportunity to give back to the community and make a real difference to the people or wildlife/animals, or to contribute to a good cause. It acquaints students with the joy of giving. Examples include: first aid, visiting and supporting people in need, volunteering at hospitals, sports coaching, charity work, etc. Physical Recreation Physical Recreation, both individually and within a team, is a fun and healthy way of developing a real sense of achievement outside the classroom, instilling enthusiasm and feeling of wellbeing. Examples include: Ball Sports, Athletics, Water Sports, Winter Sports, Martial Arts, Animal Sports, etc. Skill The Award encourages students to learn something new as a part of the process. Whether their interests lie in skiing or photography, the Award allows them to explore their passions. Examples include: Music, Arts and Crafts, Nature and the Environment, Communication, Games and Sports and related skills, etc. The Adventurous Journey The Adventurous Journey section is about undertaking a team journey or expedition. Participants plan, train for and undertake a journey with a purpose in an unfamiliar environment. Students spend 2 days and 1 night away completing around 12 hours of purposeful effort in total. Sunmarke Gavel (Toastmasters Club ) “If you can speak, you can influence. If you can influence, you can change lives.” Toastmasters International, which has a legacy of 98 years will undoubtedly change your child’s life! At Sunmarke Gavel club, which is an affiliate of Toastmasters International, your child will get access to an International Acclaimed Public Speaking programme that will help your child get adequate public speaking skills for boosting their confidence and leadership. The program is open to students between the age of 12 to 18 years. Volunteering Opportunities Volunteering is one of the greatest gifts we can give others. Sunmarke’s student volunteers work closely with the Inclusion Department at the School to learn necessary skills to coach and assist their “buddies” during training sessions. This peer-coaching programme draws upon our school’s core values and Positive Education ethos whereby confidence, physical skills and social communication skills for our athletes are built upon. 1 / 11 Facebook Twitter Pinterest

Advanced Level qualifications (known as A-Levels) are individual subject based qualifications. They are one option available to students who are looking to study at university. With A-Levels being standalone qualifications, there is no requirement on subject combinations and students’ only constraint is the combinations available within the school timetable. A-Levels are graded from A*-E. What does this Pathway look like? Students will usually take 3 or 4 A-Levels and this would be what universities would be looking for as offers are based mainly on 3 A-Level grades. If you are debating which subjects to choose, we recommend you start with 4 A-Levels so you can have a range to begin with which you can narrow down later. Students will receive 6 lessons per subject each week with most subjects being 100% examination-based. Subjects either fit into the category of modular A-Levels or linear A-Levels. In modular subjects, students will take up to three exams in Year 12 and up to three in Year 13 whereas, with linear A-Levels, students complete all exams at the end of Year 13. How does this Pathway lead to University? A-Levels are internationally recognised qualifications which will give you access to the most competitive universities worldwide. While taking A-Levels would give you the necessary prerequisites with regards to subjects, you may need to take further tests in English in order to study at universities where courses are delivered in English. In addition, students wishing to study certain subjects worldwide need to review the Mathematics requirements for entry into the university of their choice. What skills will I develop? Taking a combination of A-Levels will allow you to specialise in a particular area post 16 as opposed to waiting until you begin university. With few subjects having coursework components, there is a lot of focus on exam skills. However, there is the option of taking the Extended Project Qualification (EPQ) in order to develop your academic writing and research skills. Furthermore, the EPQ is a perfect opportunity for you to demonstrate and develop your interest in an area you want to go on to study at university; competitive universities are always looking for examples of students pursuing their academic passions outside of the classroom. Whether it be the other EPQ or another opportunity, we recommend you find an outlet to explore your passions through extra-curricular activities. 1 / 11 Facebook Twitter Pinterest

Employment What are BTECs? Short for Business and Technology Education Council, BTECs are a practical-based, vocational qualification which offers the same equivalence to A-Levels when converted into UCAS points. Many industry sectors have a set of National Occupational Standards that professionals must follow. The learning content of BTECs is built around these National Occupational Standards, which is why BTECs are recognised as valuable qualifications. They provide the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a field or subject and are an excellent alternative to the more theory focused A-Levels or subjects on the IB Diploma Programme. What does this Pathway look like? BTECs are taught through application with students often going on educational visits and meeting industry specialists as well as completing one week of work experience in Year 12. Assessments are via regular coursework and projects throughout the 2-year course. If you know you don’t excel in exam conditions, BTECs can relieve this pressure, spreading out the work that dictates your final grade as 100% of your final grade will come from these coursework components. Students are able to take a combination of BTECs and A-Levels in order to have a balance between hands on learning whilst also taking more traditional subjects. How does this Pathway lead to University? BTECs are equivalent to A-Levels in terms of applications to universities. However, there are some universities which don’t accept these qualifications so you would need to research the different countries you would like to apply for in order to ensure you meet the admissions criteria for your desired destination. What skills will I develop? BTECs truly prepare students for the real world, offering them practical skills to be successful in the industry of their choosing. If you enjoy practical learning and want to study a specialised range of subjects, BTECs are the perfect option for you. Within each subject, more technical skills are developed; for example, we are very proud of our BTEC Media courses that allow students to create using hi-tech equipment as students learn how to get the most out of this technology. 1 / 11 Facebook Twitter Pinterest

mission of the International Baccalaureate Organisation (IBO)’s programmes is to “develop inquiring, knowledgeable and caring young people who help to create a better and more peaceful world through education that builds intercultural understanding and respect.” Sunmarke offers the IB Diploma Programme as this mission aligns with our own to “Nurture the next generation of change-makers for a better tomorrow.” Through its exceptional academic and non-academic initiatives, our school grooms our students to use their education to positively influence their communities. Find out more about the details of the IB Diploma Programme at Sunmarke. What is the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme? The International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (IBDP) is a holistic programme which gives you a broad post 16 education whilst also allowing you to specialise in three subjects. You will take three Standard Level subjects and three Higher Level subjects as well as the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Creativity, Activity and Service Programme (CAS). Each subject is graded from 1-7 with the diploma core (Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay) giving 3 more points depending on the combination of grades in these components. Students must achieve a minimum total of 24 points to pass the Diploma Programme. What does this Pathway look like? Each week you will receive lessons in your 6 subjects (typically 4 lessons for higher level and 3 for standard level) as well as lessons in Theory of Knowledge (TOK). You will also receive sessions to develop writing and research skills needed for the Extended Essay. This is a piece of academic writing where you choose the subject, topic and research question to produce an answer in a 4,000 word research report. The CAS programme is a non-graded component which encourages students to set objectives in creative, active and service experiences outside of the classroom. Each subject has a coursework component worth at least 20% meaning the whole grade does not rest on the final exams. How does this Pathway lead to University? An internationally recognised qualification, the IBDP will give you access to the most competitive universities worldwide. With the DP developing more than just subject knowledge, universities see it as a perfect higher education preparation programme. To Find The Right Career Pathway Specialist One-to-One Support Sunmarke has two full-time Careers Counsellors, who, along with Form Tutors and the Head of 6 th Form, advise students on their higher education and career path. Students works closely with these experts and parents are always welcome to speak to our Careers and University team to find a pathway suitable for their child. Through conversations and research, students can find their calling and a pathway of study that excites and enthuses. Read below to see the different opportunities and platforms we use in order to help students get excited about education outside of the Sunmarke classrooms. UNIFROG Unifrog is the career and university platform that is used at Sunmarke School. It’s an impartial, user-friendly platform that helps students to research their future pathways. It contains a repository of career lessons, information on pathways, universities around the world, CV builder, personality tests, and links to MOOCs (online courses). Unifrog is useful for students in their last four years of study but can be accessed and used by all in Secondary. Students can use the platform to start to explore the different post 18 pathways and the application process for their chosen route. Careers lessons in Y12 focus on psychometric testing, university and career research and to start working on application requirements such as personal statements and US university essays. We encourage all families to explore this platform together as early as possible in order to start the conversation as to where a student may study as well as what the course requirements are in order to make sure the right combination of subjects are being chosen post 16. There are many factors that go into shortlisting universities such as location, size, tuition fees or university housing to name just a few; with all this choice, it is important to narrow down to specific countries in Year 12 so the application process is not overwhelming in Year 13. Students work one-on-one with the university careers counsellors who assist and guide students through every step of the application process. University Destinations Sunmarke students achieve their first choice university destinations which has included UK Russel Group schools, and top Worldwide destinations such as the Imperial College London, NYU, University of Amsterdam, Bocconi, Carnegie Mellon, UCLA, UC San Diego, Georgia Tech, The University of Toronto, McGill and University of Edinburgh. This policy sets out how career activities are delivered at school and what stakeholders can expect. Programme Future-Ready Learning in Our SPACE-X Innovation Lab Programme Overview At Sunmarke School, the STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, Mathematics) Signature Programme transforms students into inventors, engineers, designers, and problem-solvers through immersive, real-world learning. Anchored in our state-of-the-art SPACE-X Innovation and Design Thinking Lab, the programme encourages experimentation, collaboration, and creativity from EYFS to Year 11. Who It’s For All students from EYFS through Year 11 — regardless of prior technical knowledge. Support is available for all learning needs, including Students of Determination. Learning Journey EYFS & KS1 (Ages 3–7): Discovery-based play, early coding, foundational design skills KS2 (Ages 7–11): Engineering challenges, collaborative builds, STEAM fairs KS3–KS4 (Ages 11–16): Advanced prototyping, mechanical systems, venture incubation, AI programming What Makes It Unique Integration of Stanford Design Thinking methodology Dedicated SPACE-X Lab with 3D printers, robotics, electronics, and fabrication zones Hands-on prototyping, AI, and entrepreneurial ventures Industry mentorship and venture incubators Seamless integration with subjects like English, Business, Maths, and Art Facilities & Resources SPACE-X Innovation Lab with professional-grade tools Design Thinking Labs Digital media and design studios Electronics and robotics workstations Maker spaces and 3D fabrication labs Signature Opportunities Shark Tank-style pitch competitions Real-world product launches through the Venture Incubator Industry expert mentorship and career shadowing STEAM showcases and student exhibitions Student Outcomes Readiness for careers in innovation, tech, engineering, design, and entrepreneurship Pathways to GCSE, A-Level, IB, and BTEC qualifications in relevant fields Enhanced creativity, analytical thinking, and collaboration skills Next Steps Book a lab tour, attend our annual STEAM showcase, or speak to our coordinators to explore how your child can engage with innovation at every stage of their learning. school uniform creates a sense of unity and pride in the school community, with students understanding that they are part of one big family. Hence it has been made mandatory for all pupils to wear the prescribed school uniform. The uniform and other accessories can be purchased from the Sunmarke Uniform Store located within the school premises. Parents can also place an order through our Online Uniform Store. Here’s how: Visit our Sunmarke Online Uniform Store to select and order uniform items and/or accessories. You may pay online and have the items delivered or pick them up from the Uniform Shop at the school building. Sixth Form Uniform Policy Download Here are some other rules and dos & don’ts regarding appearance and dressing in the school: Students must be neatly dressed in ironed clothes and maintain a clean appearance. Extreme hairstyles and colours are not allowed. Students wearing trousers must wear a black belt. Parents should provide an apron for Art & Craft class. Shoulder length hair must be tied up for swimming and other practical lessons such as Art and Crafts. Colourful nail polish is not allowed. Students must wear black leather shoes and dark blue socks. For safety reasons, shoes should be flat with closed tops and laces or Velcro straps. Heels and boot-style shoes are not allowed. All items of uniform must be marked with your child’s name. Jewellery is not permitted for students with the exception of small stud earrings for girls or jewellery which is required to be worn for religious purposes. These must be either removed or covered with tape by the parent on the day of PE. Students of Key Stage 2 and above are allowed and encouraged to wear a watch to school.
